h1: The 7 Best Cordless Phones Under $500 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Cordless Phones Under $500: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven cordless phones under $500, from five-handset call-blocking systems to a two-line business set and amplified senior phones.
summary: The Panasonic KX-TGF975B is the best overall pick, with five handsets, call blocking and Bluetooth to a cell phone. The VTech IS8151-5 wins on range and expandability, and the AT&T DLP73590 is the strongest home-office choice. The AT&T TL88102 handles two lines, and the Panasonic KX-TGM420W is the pick for hearing needs.
intro: A budget of $500 for a cordless phone is far more than the category needs, which is the first thing worth knowing. Nearly every feature that matters sits in the $100-200 bucket, so spending more rarely buys better calls, only a more specialized system such as a two-line business set.

We reviewed seven models and ranked them from their spec sheets and listings: handset count, call blocking, range claims, expansion, answering system and special accessibility features. The goal is to match each phone to a real household, not to chase the highest price.

products.name: Panasonic Cordless Phone with Answering Machine, Advanced Call Block, Link2Cell Bluetooth, One-Ring Scam Alert, 2-Way Recording, Spam/Robocall Protection and 5 Handsets - KX-TGF975B
products.verdict: The most complete system here, with strong scam protection.
products.description:
This Panasonic bundle includes five handsets, an answering machine, Link2Cell Bluetooth, a one-ring scam alert, two-way recording and spam or robocall protection. It sits in the $100-200 bucket.

It leads the list because it pairs a full handset set with the broadest scam-blocking toolkit. Against the VTech below, you get more call-screening features, while the VTech has the longer documented range.

Buy it if robocalls are your main frustration and you have a multi-room home. The caveat is that five handsets are more than a small apartment needs.
cons: More handsets than small homes need
products.skipIf: You only need one or two handsets.

products.name: VTech IS8151-5 Super Long Range 5 Handset DECT 6.0 Cordless Phone for Home with Answering Machine, 2300 ft Range, Call Blocking, Bluetooth, Headset Jack, Power Backup, Intercom, Expandable to 12 HS
products.verdict: A 2300 ft range claim and room to grow to 12 handsets.
products.description:
Five handsets, a stated 2300 ft range, power backup, a headset jack and Bluetooth, expandable to 12 handsets. It lands in the $100-200 bucket.

It ranks second since the scam-blocking features are less detailed than the Panasonic's, though the range and expansion are better documented. The power backup lets the base work during an outage.

Suits large properties or a home with a workshop or garage. Range claims are for open space, so walls will reduce them.
products.idealFor: Large properties that need long range.
products.skipIf: Your home is small and one floor.

products.name: AT&T 5-Handset DECT 6.0 Cordless Home and Business Phone with Answering Machine, 5" Color Display, One-Touch Shortcut, Conference, Intercom, Smart Call Blocker, Bluetooth Connect to Cell - DLP73590
products.verdict: Business-style features with a 5 inch color display.
products.description:
Five handsets, a 5 inch color display, conference calling, intercom, a Smart Call Blocker and Bluetooth connection to a cell phone. It is priced in the $100-200 bucket.

It ranks third because its strengths are display and office features, not range or scam alerts, which the first two picks cover better. The conference function is the standout for a home office.

Choose it for a work-from-home line that needs conferencing and a big screen. Home users who just want basic calls will not use the extras.
products.idealFor: Home offices that run conference calls.
products.skipIf: You want a basic, low-cost handset.

products.name: AT&T TL88102BK DECT 6.0 2-Line Expandable Cordless Phone with Answering System and Dual Caller ID/Call Waiting, 3 Handsets, Black
products.verdict: The only true two-line phone here, for small business use.
products.description:
A 2-line DECT 6.0 system with an answering system, dual Caller ID and call waiting, and three handsets. It sits in the $200-500 bucket, the highest in this roundup.

It ranks fourth since most households do not need two lines, and the call-blocking tools are thinner than on the top picks. Its value shows when you manage two lines at once, such as a home line and a business line.

Buy it for a small office or a shop. Home users can save money with the Panasonic or AT&T five-handset kits.
products.skipIf: You only have one phone line.

products.name: Panasonic Cordless Phone, 1 Handset Amplified Wireless Phone with Slow Talk, 40dB Volume Boost, 100dB Loud Visual Ringer, Hearing Aid Compatibility, Large Screen and Backlit Keypad - KX-TGM420W
products.verdict: A single amplified handset with a loud ringer and slow talk.
products.description:
One handset with a 40dB volume boost, a 100dB loud visual ringer, Slow Talk, hearing aid compatibility, a large screen and a backlit keypad. It is in the $100-200 bucket.

It ranks fifth only because it is a one-handset phone, so it cannot cover a house. Within its niche, nothing else here offers the same amplification and visual ringer.

Best for someone with hearing loss who needs clearer, louder calls. If you want several handsets, pair a different base with this one.
products.idealFor: People with hearing loss who need amplified calls.

products.name: AT&T GL2101-2 DECT 6.0 2-Handset Cordless Phone with Call Block & Caller ID, Full-Duplex Speakerphone, 2" White Backlit Display, Lighted Keypad, Graphite & Black
products.verdict: A straightforward pair of handsets at a low price.
products.description:
Two handsets with call blocking, Caller ID, a full-duplex speakerphone, a 2 inch backlit display and a lighted keypad, in the $50-100 bucket.

It ranks sixth because it has no answering machine listed, and it covers fewer rooms than the five-handset kits above. What it gives is a low entry price for a typical home.

Choose it for an apartment or small house where two handsets are enough. Larger homes should step up.
products.idealFor: Apartments and small homes on a budget.
products.skipIf: You want an answering machine built in.

products.name: VTech VG231-4 DECT 6.0 Cordless Phone, 4-Handset
products.verdict: Four handsets for the cost of a basic pair.
products.description:
A four-handset DECT 6.0 set in the $50-100 bucket. The listing is brief, naming the handset count and the DECT 6.0 standard.

It ranks last since few other features are documented, so there is less to compare against the call-blocking and scam tools above. The advantage is plain: four handsets at a very low spend.

Good for a family that wants phones in several rooms without extras. Read the full listing for answering machine and call block details before buying.
products.idealFor: Families who want phones in many rooms cheaply.

whatMatters.detail: Each handset charges on its own base and acts as an extension. More handsets mean fewer missed calls across rooms but a higher price. Count the rooms you actually use and look for the handset number in the product title.

Built-in blocking can stop known spam numbers and warn you about one-ring scams. It matters because older callers are common targets. Look for the words call block, robocall protection or scam alert in the listing.
DECT 6.0 phones claim a range in open space, and walls cut it substantially. A bigger claimed range gives more margin in a large house. Treat figures such as 2300 ft as an upper bound.
A built-in machine saves messages without a voicemail service. Some budget sets omit it. Check the bullet points for answering machine or answering system.

Volume boost, hearing aid compatibility and visual ringers help those with hearing loss. Without them, calls can be hard to follow. Look for specific numbers such as 40dB, not just words like clear sound.

faq.q: Do cordless phones still need a landline?
faq.a: Most DECT base stations connect to a phone jack, so yes unless a model offers Bluetooth to a cell phone, as the Panasonic and AT&T DLP73590 do. Check the connection type before buying.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake buyers make?
faq.a: Overbuying handsets or underbuying range. Count your rooms first, then check how far the base needs to reach.

faq.q: Is the $200-500 two-line phone worth it?
faq.a: Only if you truly use two lines. A five-handset Panasonic or AT&T kit provides more for a household.

faq.q: How do I set up extra handsets?
faq.a: Place each handset on its charger, then register it to the base following the on-screen steps. Charge them fully first.

faq.q: How long do cordless phone batteries last?
faq.a: Rechargeable batteries wear down over a few years. Replace them with the correct type when talk time drops.

faq.q: Do I need a power backup?
faq.a: Cordless phones normally stop working when power is lost. A model with a backup like the VTech IS8151-5 helps, though a corded phone is the only guaranteed fallback.

finalTake: The Panasonic KX-TGF975B is the best buy for most households under $500, with five handsets and the strongest scam protection. Choose the VTech IS8151-5 for a big property, the AT&T DLP73590 for a home office, and the Panasonic KX-TGM420W if hearing is a concern. Spend near $500 only for a true two-line need.
